llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed VMware audit and policy helper that stores local audit/config data and has operator-controlled bypass behavior, but I found no hidden execution, exfiltration, or deceptive behavior in the artifacts.

dimensions.detail: The skill checks selected environment-variable presence for agent labeling and supports VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a documented operator escape hatch; this is sensitive but clearly disclosed and operationally scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv to install the vmware-policy package and requires Bash plus vmware-audit/uvx binaries; the artifact discloses the package, version examples, source repository, and that this skill exposes no MCP tools itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions describe when to use the CLI/library and include guidance for authors; I found no attempts to override evaluator/user safety rules or hidden agent redirection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent local files under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME for audit.db, rules.yaml, and undo.db, with documented permissions and rotation; no cron, service, startup hook, sudo use, or unauthorized persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is audit logging, optional policy checks, and sanitization for VMware skill family tools; local audit records can include sensitive operational data, but that is disclosed and aligned with the purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want VMware skill activity logged locally and understand that audit.db may contain sensitive inventory, configuration, parameters, and results. Restrict access to ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME, review exports before sharing them, configure deny rules if you expect enforcement, and avoid leaving VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 set in the MCP host environment.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig/token/password references are redaction examples and sensitive-result handling, not credential-file access or credential theft behavior.
[PE2] expected: The chmod examples set user-owned ~/.vmware and audit.db permissions; they do not invoke sudo or request root privileges.
[RA2] expected: Persistent ~/.vmware files are the disclosed local audit/config storage for this policy tool, not an unauthorized backdoor or session persistence mechanism.
[EA2] expected: The cited text recommends policy checks and routing human approval through vmware-pilot; it does not auto-authorize destructive operations by itself.
[SQP-2] expected: VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 is a real safeguard bypass risk, but it is documented as a break-glass operator switch, auditing remains enabled, and the guidance says to restrict and unset it.
[E3] expected: The ls command is a troubleshooting check for ~/.vmware/rules.yaml mtime, not broad filesystem enumeration or exfiltration.
